summary.text: 再 is used chiefly to mean “again” or “a second time.” Its ancient construction is disputed, with proposals linking it to fish, cord-making, or the idea of one act yielding two.

formation.text: The formation remains disputed. One historical account treats the graph as 一 with an abbreviated 冓 and explains it as one act yielding two; other proposals see a fish-related graph or a cord-making tool. None establishes a definitive component analysis.

history.text: Oracle-bone forms are reported in fragmentary, unclear contexts. Bronze examples are reported with the meanings “again” or “a second time,” and also “two,” but the relation between the early contexts and these uses is unclear. The selected seal-script-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact or a record of how the graph developed.

Historical variant forms are documented, but the available record does not establish a complete dated sequence leading to the modern standard shape or support a claim that it arose through corruption.

uncertainties.text: The graph’s original referent and the identities and roles of its visible parts remain unresolved. The fish, cord-tool, and “one act yielding two” accounts are competing proposals; none is established as the origin.
Some Warring States forms include 二 or 口. 二 may contribute the meaning “two,” but it may also be decorative, and this does not show that 二 occurs as a meaningful component in every form.
The earliest documented use and the full chronology of meanings remain unresolved; absolute dates for the cited bronze examples are not supplied.

senses.text: Bronze inscriptions are reported using 再 to mean “again” or “a second time.” The evidence does not establish whether this use preceded “two.”
A bronze inscription is reported using 再 to mean “two.” Its priority relative to the bronze use “again” or “a second time” is unresolved.
再 is currently used to mean “again” or “twice.” The evidence does not establish a complete sequence connecting these current meanings to the early uses.

senses.period: Warring States manuscript; absolute date unresolved
senses.text: A Guodian slip may use 再 to write 在. If so, the graph was reused for a different word on the proposed basis of a sound similarity, rather than because 再’s meaning developed into 在. The reading comparison needed to demonstrate that match is not supplied.

limitations.text: The reported early uses do not establish which sense came first, when the spoken word 再 was first used, or a complete chronology linking early and current meanings.
The proposed use of 再 to write 在 is uncertain, and the evidence does not provide historical readings that demonstrate a sound match.

overview.text: 再 commonly means “again” or “a second time.” Its ancient construction is disputed, so the modern-looking strokes cannot be confidently assigned original meanings.
